title: High-NA productivity complicates die height design
gist: This short SemiWiki forum post says High-NA scanner throughput depends on how many die rows fit within the 33 mm field height. Die heights that do not divide the field evenly cost at least 10% productivity or require stitching, and anything over 16.5 mm always needs stitching. The post says this forces Intel to treat die height as a design target, makes the 12-inch mask urgent, and is already a complication for DRAM makers heading toward 6 mm dies. The record lists Xebec as author, but the text appears under the name of moderator Fred Chen.

insights.claim: High-NA scanner productivity depends on how many row scans fit in the 33 mm field height, a point shown at the 2023 IMEC Technology Forum. Throughput is best when an even number of die rows fits within 33 mm.
insights.speaker: Xebec
insights.so_what: High-NA economics per wafer depend on the chip layout, not only on what the scanner can do.
insights.quote: The best case is when an even number of rows fits within 33 mm.

insights.claim: At High-NA die heights that do not divide the field evenly, scanner productivity drops by at least 10%, and some cases require stitching. Any die taller than 16.5 mm always requires stitching, so designs fall into narrow die-height bins.
insights.speaker: Xebec
insights.so_what: The throughput penalty raises High-NA cost per layer for large-die products such as AI accelerators.
insights.quote: For more than 16.5 mm, stitching is always required.
insights.locator: The number of row scans in

insights.claim: The post argues that a 12-inch mask size is urgently needed. Until then, current High-NA users such as Intel will have to treat die height as an explicit design target.
insights.speaker: Xebec
insights.so_what: Intel, as the lead High-NA adopter, faces design constraints, and a 12-inch mask standard could become a catalyst for the mask and lithography supply chain.
insights.quote: The 12" mask size definitely cannot come soon enough

insights.claim: DRAM makers are heading toward die heights of about 6 mm, so stitching is already a major complication for them in adopting High-NA.
insights.speaker: Xebec
insights.so_what: Field-size friction could slow or complicate High-NA adoption by memory makers.
